title: Join the two intake routes onto one finding identity
body:
Two routes put playtest findings into `intake/queue/`, and they do not share an identity space, so
the same defect can occupy the queue twice under unrelated ids.

**Route A — corpus triage.** `bin/triage.ts` clusters session records, mints
`ticketId({kind, location, fingerprint})`, writes `qa/tickets/`, and `reconcileTicketSubmissions`
keys the intake submission on that ticket id (`submissionId({source, kind, key: ticket.ticket_id})`).

**Route B — fleet review / `npm run submit`.** A reviewer compiles a fleet run and files a
submission directly, with an id that is not derived from any cluster.

Neither can recognise the other's finding, because only one of them is computing a cluster identity
at all.

## Observed instance

`intake/queue/P1-playtest-56b3d1a6260af50c.json` — "Albany Rowan docket appears without executable
job options", 3 independent Terra reports on build `f9b5c73d`, area `src/world/session_local_view.ts`,
filed 2026-09-01 through route B. It has **no file in `qa/tickets/`** and its evidence refs point at
`ai-runs/fleet/terra-100-f9b5-copy-20260831/summary.json` and a review compile.

On 2026-09-05 two live `claude_code` sessions (`16bfc47f69d0`, `4f1a4a92dfb3`, both
`runner_enforced`, build `2da50f33`) independently hit the same defect: the docket is listed, and
`work_overworld_session_job` rejects it demanding an `option_id` that no `job_choices` data ever
exposes. Route A clustered them correctly into one ticket — `S2-bug-3c86bd6dd9e5109f` @ `albany_city`,
`report_count: 2` — under an identity with no relationship to `56b3d1a6260af50c`.

So the queue is on course to carry two items for one defect, and the second one's evidence does not
strengthen the first.

## Why this is worth fixing rather than tolerating

The cost is not the single duplicate. It is that **every finding the Terra-era fleet already filed
will be re-filed as new work the moment the live loop rediscovers and corroborates it** — precisely
the findings most likely to recur, since they were real enough to be filed once. The queue's ranking
then sees two weak items where the evidence supports one strong one, and a human reading the queue
cannot tell that the second is the first with more witnesses.

## Options

1. **Compute the same identity on route B.** Have the fleet-review submission path derive
   `ticketId` from the cluster it was compiled from, so both routes land on one key. Cleanest, and
   makes corroboration across routes automatic. Requires route B to carry a cluster, which the
   review compile already has.
2. **Match on the way in.** Teach `reconcileTicketSubmissions` to look for an existing open
   submission with the same normalized location plus `area` before minting a new id, and attach the
   evidence to it. Cheaper, but a heuristic — and a wrong match silently merges two defects, which
   is worse than a duplicate.
3. **Accept and let it self-heal** (the current decision). Legacy route-B items age out after
   `STALE_AFTER_BUILDS`; the cost is temporary pairs. Reasonable while the queue is small and the
   fleet route is dormant, and it costs nothing to revisit if the pairs start crowding the queue.

Option 1 is the one worth building if this is ever picked up; option 2 should be resisted unless the
match is exact, because over-merging hides a defect while duplication merely wastes attention.

## Related

- `8d3d6658909e0d86` — clustering splits (queue).
- `dcaefa368898e77c` — no-location findings never corroborate; addressed by the
  `qa-unmapped-identity` patch.

evidence.summary: Corpus triage and direct submission mint unrelated ids for the same finding; observed on the Rowan docket defect (56b3d1a6260af50c vs S2-bug-3c86bd6dd9e5109f).
